messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts detected for region-us-east-1. spike started 1782301000. paging oncall. :rotating_light:
devon (oncall): acknowledged, I'm on it. grabbing logs and current queues.
sre-lead: thanks. early hypothesis: batch scheduler queue backlog -> headlock on low-priority lanes. symptoms: sustained increase in per-request latency, many requests hitting gateway 504s and 502s.
elaine (runtime): seeing scheduler queue length jump on the telemetry page: https://telemetry/redwood/queues?env=prod&region=us-east-1 — tail ~1800, head latency rising. KV cache growth also spiking, but suspect batching windows.
matt (gateway): also seeing proxy 5xxs from runner pool (runner-*) and many upstream timeouts: 
```
proxy error: upstream read timeout after 30s
handler: 502 Bad Gateway
```

devon (oncall): quick mitigations I'm going to try now: 1) reduce batching window to 5ms for region-us-east-1, 2) drain low-priority queues (mark priority=low as suspend), 3) scale scheduler-pool +2 instances. will run one at a time and report.
sre-lead: thumbs up. prefer throttle low-priority rather than drop customer requests. do we have a safe toggle?
elaine (runtime): yes, can flip quickflag: BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS for region-us-east-1. also can flip SCHEDULER_QUEUE_WEIGHT for low-priority to 0. commands below: 
```
# reduce batching window
redwoodctl config set --env prod --region us-east-1 BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS=5
# suspend low-priority routing
redwoodctl config set --env prod --region us-east-1 SCHEDULER_QUEUE_WEIGHT.low=0
# scale scheduler
redwoodctl scale schedulers --env prod --region us-east-1 +2
```

devon (oncall): running BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS change now. patch id: cfg-1782301111-01.
incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE applied by devon (oncall) at 1782301202: cfg-1782301111-01 (BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS=5)
devon (oncall): monitoring... initial tail latency drops slightly, but still seeing some 5xx. proceeding to suspend low-priority routing.
incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE applied by devon (oncall) at 1782301318: cfg-1782301111-02 (SCHEDULER_QUEUE_WEIGHT.low=0)
matt (gateway): after the suspend, proxy 5xx rate down from 15% -> 7% in last 2m. still seeing timeouts spaced every ~20s from a small subset of runner instances.
elaine (runtime): scaling schedulers now. started 2 more nodes. rollout progressing.
devon (oncall): starting a rolling restart of runner pool nodes showing highest error rates (runner-03*, runner-07*). will cordon them first.
sre-lead: callout: customer-impact summary for support: some customers in us-east-1 experiencing timeouts and 5xx for text generation endpoints between ~1782301000 and mitigation window. impact window may still be open for a subset.
jess (support): copying customers in affected orgs. drafting status note: "We are addressing intermittent 5xx errors and timeouts in us-east-1; mitigating now." Will include ETA 15-30m pending metrics.
pager-duty-bot: Escalation: oncall handoff recommended if incident not resolved in 30m.
elaine (runtime): logs show a small set of requests with very long decoding times causing KV cache hot entries: 
```
[1782301215] request_id=abc123 tokens=2048 decode_ms=28740 kv_cache_size=1.2GB
[1782301220] request_id=def456 tokens=1900 decode_ms=26300 kv_cache_size=1.25GB
```
these long-decoding requests are holding slots and blocking batching groups.

devon (oncall): can we set a per-request token cap to reduce decode tail for now? if we cap at 1024 tokens we should free some runtime.
elaine (runtime): yes, we can set REQUEST_TOKEN_CAP=1024 per-region as emergency. applying: 
```
redwoodctl config set --env prod --region us-east-1 REQUEST_TOKEN_CAP=1024
```
incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE applied by devon (oncall) at 1782301650: cfg-1782301111-03 (REQUEST_TOKEN_CAP=1024)
matt (gateway): after token cap, we see tail decode times drop and backlog reduces. 5xx now 2.1% and trending down.
sre-lead: good. continue monitoring for 10m. if stable, prepare for partial rollback of low-priority suspend to restore capacity.
devon (oncall): doing a staggered re-enable of low-priority at 10% weight to avoid sudden load. 
incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE applied by devon (oncall) at 1782302100: cfg-1782301111-04 (SCHEDULER_QUEUE_WEIGHT.low=0.1)
jess (support): updating customers: "Errors reduced; mitigation in progress. We will update again in 30m."
elaine (runtime): telemetry now shows queue tail down to ~120, head latency normalized for most lanes. KV cache growth stabilized.

sre-lead: assessment: primary trigger = long-running, large-token decoding requests causing slot monopolization -> head-of-line blocking in scheduler queues. Contributing factor: batching window previously mis-tuned for this traffic mix, which increased grouping and hold times.
devon (oncall): will keep incident open and hand off in 20m to lina (oncall-next). summary for handoff: timeline, config changes (list), outstanding tasks: 1) continue monitoring for regression, 2) run targeted collector to find top long-request clients, 3) coordinate with runtime team for safer rate limits and per-client backpressure.
lina (oncall-next): ack, I'll take the handoff at 1782303600 if still open. please paste short playbook in thread.
devon (oncall): pasting quick playbook: 
- preserve incident log link: https://incidents/redwood/1782301111
- rollback sequence: revert REQUEST_TOKEN_CAP only after KV cache stable
- recovery: do not re-enable full low-priority weight >0.5 until 30m of stable metrics
- followups: assign RCA to eng-runtime, add regression test for large-token tail.

incident-bot: PAGING: handoff scheduled to lina (oncall-next) at 1782303600 if unresolved.

(last update) devon (oncall): handing off now to lina (oncall-next). incident stable. 5xx baseline ~0.5%, latency within SLOs. leaving open for root-cause and follow-ups.
lina (oncall-next): taking over. thanks for the summary. I'll coordinate postmortem and link to this thread. tagging eng-runtime and gateway owners for RCA.

sre-lead: next steps: ENG-RUNTIME to debug why large-token requests weren't preempted and why batching window amplified headlock. deploy safe-guards: per-request slot timeout (TIMER_SLOT_MAX_MS=20000) + early-eviction for >1500 tokens.
elaine (runtime): assigning to queue: RT-17823. ETA for investigation initial findings: 48 hours.
matt (gateway): will follow up on proxy-side circuit breakers to fail-fast earlier.
jess (support): will send final customer update summarizing root cause and mitigation plan once RCA is ready.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated (reduced errors), open for RCA and follow-up tasks. record created: INC-1782301111.
